title: auth: normalize header semantics for project/org keys, scoped tokens, CORS and request-signing headers
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Context: We have several compatibility issues around how requests are authenticated across the OpenAI-compatible proxy and the native Redwood API: project vs org-scoped keys, per-route scoped tokens, CORS preflight behavior for browser SDKs, and a fragile request-signing header (X-Redwood-Signature / X-Redwood-Nonce) handling. This PR standardizes header semantics and introduces a compatibility opt-in flag so existing customers don't break.

Changes in this PR:
- Introduce canonical header parsing in api/auth/headers.py: Accept Authorization bearer tokens, X-Redwood-Project, X-Redwood-Org, and X-Redwood-Scoped-Token. Resolve precedence: scoped token > project header > bearer token (if token has project scope). This fixes ambiguous behavior where SDKs sent both project header and bearer token and the proxy randomly preferred one.
- OpenAI compatibility layer (openai_compat/middleware.py): Ensure OpenAI-style "Authorization: Bearer <key>" continues to work, but we now map legacy project-prefixed keys to X-Redwood-Project for downstream services when compatibility flag is enabled.
- CORS: Add explicit handling for Access-Control-Allow-Credentials and Vary headers in api/http/cors.py and documented recommended browser usage in docs/api-auth.md. We tightened the default allowed origins but expose a per-tenant config to relax for legacy tenants.
- Request signing headers: normalize reading and replay protection for X-Redwood-Nonce and X-Redwood-Signature. Reject duplicate nonce reuse within a short ttl and log suspicious attempts. Added tests for replay detection.
- SDK updates: redwood-sdk-typescript change to stop sending X-Project header by default and instead detect when a project key is used and set the canonical header. The change is guarded behind a feature flag to roll out gradually.

Why: Multiple customer incidents (linked in Linear below) were traced to ambiguous auth precedence and CORS misconfig when apps used browser SDKs with embedded project keys. This PR makes precedence explicit, reduces accidental key misuse, and provides a compatibility path.

Rollout plan: feature flag controlled. Canary in staging for 48 hours, then opt-in for legacy tenants, then default enable after 2 weeks. Observability: added metrics for rejected nonces, header-precedence-used, and compatibility-mapping-ratio.

Notes for reviewers: The description above is a single continuous string. The implementation tries to avoid behavioral changes unless the compatibility flag is off; please look closely at api/auth/headers.py parsing rules and the unit tests in tests/auth/test_header_parsing.py.

c3d6f7a - cors: tighten defaults and add per-tenant override plus docs update (api/http/cors.py, docs/api-auth.md)
d4e7g8h - sdk(ts): feature-flagged project header behavior and integration tests (redwood-sdk-typescript/src/auth.ts, tests/sdk/browser-auth.test.ts)
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Please clarify precedence rules in headers.py and add explicit unit tests for combinations of bearer+project+scoped-token.
Ava Martinez: Added explicit precedence table in header parser docstring and new tests covering all combinations (see tests/auth/test_header_parsing.py).
Priya Patel: CORS tightening looks good but worried about breaking embedders. Can we gate behind tenant flag?
Ava Martinez: Yes, added per-tenant override and rollout notes in docs. We also emit a metric to track usage so SRE can monitor.
Noah Kim: Request-signing replay protection needs TTL comment and a configurable window; add an env var override
Ava Martinez: Added REDWOOD_NONCE_TTL and documented default (5m). Also exposed a metrics counter for rejected nonces.
release_notes: Standardize auth header semantics: canonical header parsing (project/org/scoped tokens), OpenAI-compat mapping opt-in flag, tightened CORS defaults with per-tenant override, and request-signing replay protection. Backwards-compatible behind feature flag; rollout planned.
notes: Observed customer incidents SUP-462 and ENG-1256 motivated this change. Monitoring dashboards added for header-precedence-used and rejected-nonces. SDK teams coordinated a staggered rollout.
